problem_statement:
[bug/security] Org managers can escalate themselves to superusers
**Expected behavior:** org manager (non superuser) should not be able to edit permissions, nor flag themselves or others are superusers.

**Actual behavior**: org manager (non superuser) are able to flag themselves or others are superusers.

This is a regression, this was working fine before, but for some reason, the user permission section in the user management admin page got duplicated and the duplicated part allows users to flag themselves as superusers or assign themselves new permissions.

See the recording below for clarification:

![users-bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/841044/137373951-d719b394-e445-414e-89d0-21cf011d5388.gif)

The second permission section is duplicated and shouldn't be there.

**We must add the following admin tests:**

- when accessing user change page as a non superuser who has permissions to edit an user:
  - ensure there's no mention of superuser at all (eg: `is_superuser`)
  - ensure user permissions are not editable
  - ensure there's only one is_active field, only one is_staff field, only one instnace of group editing
